title: The Hall Is Cleared
source: Homer, Odyssey XXII, tr. Samuel Butler (public domain)
note: Hand-staged from the text in the megaron of OD-B22-S01: Athena raises the aegis before the high seat; Odysseus, Telemachus, Eumaeus and Philoetius come up the hall from the threshold and each strikes one suitor down (keys K1a-K1d, placed inside the first turn with `after`); Leiodes runs to Odysseus's knees and is killed (K2, K2a); Phemius and Medon kneel and are spared (K3, K4); the living search the hall (K5).

keys.beat: Odysseus and his allies pursue the suitors through the hall like falcons among smaller birds
keys.text: Then Minerva held up her deadly aegis from her seat aloft in the roof, and the suitors were in a panic like a herd of cattle maddened by the gadfly; the others fell upon them like eagles from the mountains.

keys.beat: The four come up the hall
keys.text: The others fell upon them like eagles from the mountains.

keys.beat: Telemachus and Philoetius come at theirs
Leiodes clasps Odysseus's knees but is killed despite claiming innocence
keys.text: Leiodes then caught the knees of Ulysses and said, "Ulysses I beseech you have mercy upon me and spare me."
He struck him on the middle of his neck.

keys.beat: Phemius and Medon appeal for mercy and Telemachus confirms their limited complicity
keys.text: Phemius laid his lyre on the ground and clasped the knees of Ulysses. Medon crept out from under the ox hide and clasped the knees of Telemachus.

keys.beat: Odysseus spares the bard and herald and orders them into the courtyard
keys.text: "Go outside the cloisters into the outer court, you and the bard, out of the slaughter."

keys.beat: The bard and the herald go out
keys.text: The two went out of the cloisters.

keys.beat: The living search the blood-filled hall for any remaining threat
keys.text: Then Ulysses searched the whole court carefully over, to see if anyone had hidden himself and was still living.
